# 303box

> 303box is a free browser-based 16-step acid bassline and rhythm tool inspired by TB-303 / TD-3 workflows, with Web Audio preview, compact signal analysis, MIDI output and a classic Roland-style drum machine.

Canonical URL: https://303box.com/

## Core capabilities
- Program 16 acid sequencing steps.
- Choose notes from a chromatic note selector and set octave down/up, accent, slide, trigger, tie and rest states.
- Choose sawtooth or square waveform.
- Adjust tempo from 50 to 250 BPM with a hardware-style knob and seven-segment display.
- Adjust cutoff, resonance, envelope modulation, decay and accent.
- Preview patterns with the Web Audio API.
- Inspect the 303 signal with a compact oscilloscope / FFT display inside the sequencer workspace.
- Connect supported MIDI hardware through the Web MIDI API and send note messages plus optional MIDI clock.
- Program a separate 16-step drum machine with bass drum, snare, clap, tom, closed hi-hat and open hi-hat parts.
- Select 808-, 909- and 606-style synthesized drum character where available.
- Start drums independently or synchronize their start to the next step 1 of the 303 sequencer.
- Randomize drum patterns with adjustable density.
- Mix 303 and drum output independently; both default to 80 percent.
- Export the visible 303 pattern editor as a JPG.
- Store working sessions locally in the browser.

## Languages
- English
- Turkish

- Sequencer: https://303box.com/#sequencer

## Historical coverage
The site includes a sourced TB-303 timeline covering Roland/Tadao Kikumoto, Phuture (DJ Pierre, Spanky, Herb J), Ron Hardy, A Guy Called Gerald, Hardfloor and Josh Wink. The drum reference briefly explains the TR-808, TR-909 and TR-606, including the TR-606's original role as a companion to the TB-303.
